title: Routing Policy and Firewall Filters: The Complete Beginner's Guide
kicker: BEGINNER'S GUIDE · JUNOS POLICY AND FILTERS

scenes.narration: Junos has two kinds of checkpoint. One checks the packets. The other checks the routes.

scenes.heading: Airport security and customs
scenes.narration: At an airport, security screens the passengers, and customs checks the paperwork. Both follow a list of rules, from the top down. Screening checks every passenger. Customs checks the flight list. Both use terms with from and then.

scenes.heading: What can they do
scenes.narration: Each one has its own set of actions. A filter can accept, discard, reject or log a packet. A policy can accept or reject a route, and also change its attributes. A filter handles packets, and a policy handles routes. Only a policy can change a route's attributes. And a policy applies on import or export.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three misunderstandings. They're different, one works on packets and the other on routes. A reject stops the route being used, it doesn't wipe it from every table. By default Junos allows traffic unless you apply a filter.

items.wrong: Filters and policies are the same
items.right: One acts on packets, one on routes
It just stops it being used

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos policy lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Filters check packets, and policies check routes. Both read terms from the top, first match wins. Reject sends a message back, and discard stays silent. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos policy lab.
